Overview, machinery, and pathways

Serotonin (5-hydroxy-tryptamine, 5-HT) is forged from tryptophan in ∼nine bilateral raphe nuclei that straddle the midline of the pontine and medullary brain-stem. The dorsal (B7) and median (B8) raphe nuclei together supply most forebrain serotonin, while more caudal groups carpet the cerebellum, spinal cord, and autonomic nuclei. Although serotonergic somata number only on the order of 200,000, each cell grows beaded, extraordinarily ramifying axons so that a single spike volley can wet millimetres of cortex with transmitter in a few hundred milliseconds-a design that allows 5-HT to re-weight whole-brain dynamics on the fly. Modern single-cell transcriptomics and viral tracing reveal that the raphe is anything but monolithic: plate-based single-cell RNA-sequencing generated a dataset comprising eleven transcriptomically distinct serotonin neuron clusters subtypes 1, with these transcriptomic clusters differentially express a rich repertoire of neuropeptides, receptors, ion channels, and transcription factors; subtypes also project with surprising specificity to sensory, limbic, basal-ganglia, or prefrontal targets, implying parallel "micro-circuits" rather than one global spray 2, 3. A mouse atlas maps molecularly distinct serotonin neurons (Figure). The atlas maps projections of serotonin-neuron populations (Figure).

The computational power of serotonin emerges from its diverse receptor mechanisms operating across multiple timescales. The 7 general serotonin receptor classes include a total of 14 known serotonin receptors, each implementing distinct computational operations through specific G-protein coupling patterns. The 5-HT1R and 5-HT5R subtypes couple with Gi/o protein, leading to the inhibition of adenylyl cyclase (AC) activity and a reduction in cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) levels 4, while 5-HT2R couples with Gq/11 protein, stimulating phospholipase C, which leads to elevated levels of inositol triphosphate and calcium ions (Ca2+). This diversity enables serotonin to implement both fast synaptic transmission and slower paracrine signaling, with some projections form classical chemical synapses while many do not, thus contributing to the so-called paracrine or volume transmission 5.

At the synaptic level, 5-HT gates plasticity in receptor-specific ways: Gs-coupled 5-HT4/6/7 receptors raise cAMP/PKA, lower LTP thresholds, and accelerate dendritic spine maturation, whereas 5-HT1A autoinhibition or postsynaptic activation can stabilise working-memory ensembles by damping HCN-mediated noise currents.

Serotonergic neurons in the dorsal raphe fire tonically at low single-digit rates (∼1-5 Hz on average, state-dependent) and exhibit phasic, task-locked modulations to salient events, including expectancy violations. Optogenetic fMRI shows that brief activation of DRN 5-HT produces widespread BOLD increases across medial prefrontal cortex, striatum, and VTA in awake animals, whereas under isoflurane these effects are markedly reduced or inverted-consistent with projection- and receptor-specific bidirectionality (e.g., stronger 5-HT₁-mediated inhibition) 6, 7, 8.

Signaling long-horizon cost-benefit tradeoffs

Recent work refines Doya’s (2002) proposal that serotonin tunes temporal discounting by showing that subsets of dorsal raphe 5-HT neurons carry slow, predictive signals that approximate discounted state value over multi-second horizons in waiting/foraging tasks, while other subsets exhibit fast, mixed-signed responses to appetitive and aversive events 9, 10. Behaviorally, lowering central 5-HT (e.g., tryptophan depletion) reliably steepens temporal discounting and, in several RL fits, leaves learning rates and choice stochasticity comparatively less affected-consistent with a relatively specific influence on the discount parameter, though not an exclusive one. Framed as a "meta-decision variable" 11, serotonergic tone appears to encode (or regulate in proportion to) long-horizon value calibrated by resource availability and costs (time, effort, metabolic load, risk), thereby adjusting patience, persistence, quitting thresholds, and the propensity to engage model-based over model-free control. This picture, however, is mechanistically heterogeneous: receptor class (5-HT1A/1B vs 5-HT2A/2C), target circuit (PFC, striatum, accumbens, hippocampus), and timescale (phasic vs tonic) all matter, and some DRN neurons carry aversive or RPE-like components. Thus, serotonin is best viewed as a family of meta-decision control signals that bias planning depth and opportunity-cost accounting, rather than a unitary, purely ’slow value’ channel. A mouse study records raphe signals during reward seeking (Figure). The study examines activity while animals wait for reward (Figure).

In support of these computations, serotonergic neurons in the DRN and median raphe receive unusually rich context about both future payoffs and the costs of getting there:

Hypothalamic AgRP/POMC, leptin/ghrelin, insulin, orexin, and other interoceptive channels project (directly or via parabrachial nucleus/BNST/insula routes) to raphe, letting 5-HT "know" whether you can afford to wait, work, or explore. Low energy or high internal threat should compress the horizon (steepen discounting).

The anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and supplementary motor areas (SMAs)-which encode subjective effort, sunk costs, and time-on-task-send dense projections to DRN. These signals can down-weight protracted plans when predicted control costs are high.

Amygdala, BNST, periaqueductal gray (PAG), and habenula-RMTg pathways convey threat, pain, and negative surprise. These inputs let 5-HT factor prospective harm into the long-horizon estimate, often by raising patience for safe plans and lowering it when the tail risk is fat.

OFC, vmPFC, hippocampus, striatum, and VTA DA neurons provide slowly varying predictions of expected value and context/state identity. Empirically, many DRN 5-HT neurons ramp ahead of expected rewards and track discounted state value over multi-second windows, complementary to dopamine’s fast, derivative-like RPE bursts.

Locus coeruleus (NE) and basal forebrain ACh gauge the price of time (what else you could be doing) and the precision of beliefs. High tonic NE (high opportunity cost) can bias 5-HT systems to truncate horizons (switch sooner), while low NE enables the serotonin system to support long, persistent policies.

Suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) and other chronobiological inputs give serotonin a very literal clock, modulating the affordable horizon across the day (and across sleep pressure).

On top of its access to rich value, cost, threat, and interoceptive signals, serotonin’s position as a long-horizon state-value estimator reflects three additional specialties:

Slow biophysics: 5-HT neurons exhibit prominent after-depolarizations, calcium-dependent plateau potentials, metabotropic receptor kinetics, and recurrent raphe->raphe loops that naturally low-pass filter inputs. That turns fast cortical/striatal value signals into slow ramps that look like multi-second discounted value traces.

Metabotropic, diffuse, extrasynaptic signaling: 5-HT is often volume-transmitted; its receptors are mostly slow GPCRs. That pushes it toward setting global control knobs (discount, patience, planning depth, quitting thresholds) rather than encoding moment-to-moment spikes of information.

Division of labor with dopamine: It’s metabolically and computationally efficient to let DA carry the derivative (error/novelty/uncertainty) while 5-HT carries the integral (sustained value/persistence), solving a classic control problem (PD vs. I terms) at the algorithmic level.

Even if DRN computes a broadly similar "long-horizon value" signal, spatial gradients in projections, receptors, and transporters make its effects highly region-specific:

Medial/ventral DRN neurons preferentially project to limbic cortex, hippocampus, amygdala, whereas lateral "wing" DRN neurons target basal ganglia and sensorimotor territories. Thus, patience/persistence signals can be stronger for cognitive/affective control vs. action selection, or vice versa, depending on context. A mouse optogenetic-fMRI study maps responses to raphe stimulation (Figure). The study compares activation with serotonin projections (Figure).

5-HT2A receptors are enriched in association cortex (especially layer V pyramidal neurons), promoting excitation and cognitive flexibility, whereas 5-HT1A density is high in mPFC/hippocampus, producing inhibition and stability. A single ramping 5-HT waveform can therefore stabilize long-range planning circuits (via 1A) while loosening over-confident local attractors to encourage model-based reevaluation (via 2A).

5-HT1B receptors presynaptically modulate glutamate and dopamine release with a dorso-ventral gradient, letting serotonin tune exploration/exploitation differently in dorsal (habitual/model-free) vs ventral (goal-directed/model-based) striatum.

Regions with higher densities of serotonin transporters (SERT) will experience briefer, sharper 5-HT transients; low-SERT territories will see longer, more integrative signals-effectively spatially varying time constants for the same raphe output.

Mood

Phenomenologically, mood looks like the low-pass, circuit-weighted integral of serotonin’s long-horizon value estimates: when tonic 5-HT-especially in mPFC/hippocampus via 5-HT1A and 5-HT4/6/7-signals that future returns exceed opportunity costs, networks settle into an "optimistic, patient" attractor; when tone falls, or LC-NE/habenular/SCN inputs truncate the affordable horizon, the running estimate of future value collapses and mood drifts negative, yielding impatience and impulsivity.

Phasic 5-HT rides on this baseline as micro-updates, but slow GPCR kinetics, somatodendritic 5-HT1A autoreceptor feedback, and raphe->raphe recurrence set a long averaging window-explaining why SSRIs raise extracellular 5-HT rapidly yet improve mood only after weeks, when autoreceptors desensitize and downstream plasticity (e.g., BDNF upregulation, spine remodeling, hippocampal pattern separation) retunes priors away from pessimistic predictions.

Spatial/receptor gradients let the same waveform stabilize cognition (5-HT1A-heavy mPFC) or promote flexible reappraisal (5-HT2A-rich association cortex), aligning psychedelic 5-HT2A agonism’s acute emotional lability with its longer-term antidepressant plasticity. Trait-level variation in SERT expression, raphe-amygdala coupling, and metabolic/interoceptive inputs effectively lengthen or shorten serotonin’s temporal integration window, shifting baseline mood by biasing how far ahead-and how hopefully-the system looks.

Social cognition

Dense 5-HT projections blanket canonical social hubs-anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), orbitofrontal cortex, amygdala, hippocampus CA2, nucleus accumbens and medial septum-where phasic bursts or slow ramps re-weight how these nodes integrate social cues. In awake humans, sub-second microdialysis in substantia nigra shows that serotonin tracks the current value of offers during an ultimatum game, while neighbouring dopamine encodes rapid prediction-errors-evidence that 5-HT supplies a slowly integrating "state value" channel even for abstract, strategic exchanges with other people 12, 13. A human imaging study tests social-hierarchy learning (Figure). The study relates serotonin-transporter availability to social learning (Figure).

A century of ethology already hinted that the raphe sets the pecking order: elevating central 5-HT in vervet monkeys flips subordinates into alpha-like behaviour, whereas depletion has the opposite effect. Modern PET-fMRI in humans extends the story: individuals with low serotonin-transporter (SERT) availability in dorsal raphe show larger ventral-striatal signals when computing opponents’ ranks, implying that higher extracellular 5-HT dampens the neural salience-and perhaps the emotional sting-of losing status. More broadly, 5-HT1B signalling in orbitofrontal/violence circuits restrains impulsive aggression, while 5-HT2C activity in lateral habenula biases surrender when the cost of further conflict outweighs potential gain 14, 15.

Prosociality is not a monolith, and serotonin’s bidirectional control becomes obvious when one parses the behaviours. In rodents, activating dorsal-raphe -> ACC fibres via 5-HT1A/2A receptors promotes consolation grooming after a cage-mate’s distress, yet the same manipulations can blunt vicarious freezing (an empathy-like read-out), suggesting parallel channels for "soothing" versus "feeling" the other’s pain. Chemically forcing a massive 5-HT surge with MDMA shifts the balance toward affiliative approach: nucleus-accumbens release potentiates oxytocin-driven circuits and produces measurable empathy-like behaviours even in mice. Conversely, raising tonic 5-HT in the ACC can reduce empathic responses in observational-fear paradigms, underscoring receptor- and circuit-specific polarity 12.

Social memory-remembering who a conspecific is-also leans on serotonin. Median-raphe terminals that release 5-HT onto medial-septal neurons gate plasticity at septum->CA2 synapses via 5-HT1B receptors; optogenetically amplifying this signal stabilises the memory trace for familiar individuals, whereas suppressing it hastens forgetting. Such circuitry places serotonin as a molecular "notary" that certifies social encounters worth storing, dovetailing with CA2’s unique role in identity coding 16.

Finally, serotonin shapes the computations that let us navigate norms, fairness and cooperation. Acute tryptophan depletion famously makes people reject almost any unfair split in the ultimatum game; the 2024 microdialysis study reveals the flip side-higher in-situ 5-HT flattens sensitivity to inequity by keeping the integrated value signal lofty when offers are stingy. This slow, context-aware coding is well-suited for adjusting long-horizon strategies such as tit-for-tat reciprocity, and it interacts with oxytocin in nuanced ways-baseline 5-HT4-receptor binding predicts who will (or will not) show oxytocin-induced shifts in affective bias 13, 17.

In sum, serotonin supplies a suite of social control knobs: it tempers aggression and dominance drives, stamps social encounters into memory, toggles consolation versus empathy, and biases moral-economic choices toward patience and cooperation-all via projection- and receptor-specific computations layered atop the long-horizon value code detailed in the preceding section.
